skill.name: threejs-builder
skill.description: Creates Three.js web app patterns with scene setup, lighting, materials, animation loops, camera controls, and responsive rendering guidance.
skill.summary: Builds modern Three.js scenes and app patterns for interactive 3D web experiences.
skill.author: CesarAugustusGroB

security_audit.summary: Most external command and system reconnaissance alerts are false positives from Markdown formatting, JavaScript examples, and GLSL snippets. The confirmed issues are low-risk hardcoded CDN imports used by example Three.js apps, with no evidence of prompt injection or malicious intent.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer npm package imports for production examples, or clearly disclose when generated apps load modules from unpkg.
Keep dependency versions pinned and provide local bundler alternatives for Three.js addons and related libraries.

static_findings.snippet: 1. **Scene Graph First**: Everything added to `scene` renders. Use `Group` for hierarchical transfor
3. **Animation as Transformation**: Change position/rotation/scale over time using `requestAnimation
Built-in primitives cover most simple app needs. Use `BufferGeometry` only for custom shapes.
- `MeshBasicMaterial` - No lighting, flat colors. Use for: UI, wireframes, unlit effects
- `MeshStandardMaterial` - PBR lighting. Default for realistic surfaces
- `MeshPhysicalMaterial` - Advanced PBR with clearcoat, transmission. Glass, water
- `MeshNormalMaterial` - Debug, rainbow colors based on normals
- `MeshPhongMaterial` - Legacy, shininess control. Faster than Standard
- `DirectionalLight(color, intensity)` - Sun-like, parallel rays. Cast shadows
- `PointLight(color, intensity, distance)` - Light bulb, emits in all directions
- `SpotLight(color, intensity, angle, penumbra)` - Flashlight, cone of light
Why bad: Controls won't load, `THREE.OrbitControls` is undefined in modern Three.js
Better: Use `import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js'` or unpkg exampl
Better: Always call `scene.add(object)` after creating meshes/lights
Better: Default segments are usually fine. `SphereGeometry(1, 32, 16)` not `SphereGeometry(1, 128, 6
Better: Define constants at top: `const CONFIG = { color: 0x00ff88, speed: 0.001 }`
**Modern Three.js (r150+) uses ES modules from `three` package or CDN.** CommonJS patterns and globa
- **Data visualization**: Clean lines, grid helpers, clear labels

content.value_statement: Creating 3D web scenes requires careful setup, rendering, controls, and performance choices. This skill gives practical Three.js patterns for modern browser-based 3D apps.
actual_capabilities: Scaffolds modern ES module Three.js scenes with camera, renderer, resize handling, and animation loops.
Guides choices for geometries, materials, lights, colors, and camera controls.
Provides patterns for particles, product viewers, model loading, shaders, post-processing, and physics references.
Applies performance guidance for pixel ratio caps, geometry reuse, instancing, and shadow settings.
Explains common setup mistakes and modern import paths for Three.js r150 and newer.
limitations: Does not provide hosted 3D assets, textures, or model files.
Generated scenes still require browser testing for framing, motion, and device performance.
CDN examples depend on third-party availability unless converted to local npm imports.
Complex physics, shaders, and loaders may require project-specific tuning.

use_cases.title: Prototype a 3D landing scene
use_cases.description: Create a responsive animated scene with lighting, motion, and a clear focal object.

use_cases.title: Design a product viewer
use_cases.description: Plan an orbit-controlled viewer with practical camera placement, lighting, and material guidance.

use_cases.title: Teach Three.js fundamentals
use_cases.description: Explain scene graphs, primitives, materials, lights, and animation using small focused examples.

prompt_templates.title: Create a starter scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple Three.js scene with one animated object, responsive resizing, basic lighting, and clear setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add camera controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Add orbit-style camera controls to my Three.js scene and keep the animation smooth on desktop and mobile browsers.

prompt_templates.title: Build a product viewer
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Three.js product viewer with realistic lighting, PBR materials, orbit controls, and a clean responsive layout.

prompt_templates.title: Create an advanced visual system
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a performant Three.js scene using model loading, post-processing, instancing, and clear performance safeguards.

output_examples.input: Create a rotating low-poly planet scene for a portfolio page.
output: A full-screen 3D scene with a low-poly planet, soft lighting, subtle rotation, and responsive camera framing.
Performance notes covering pixel ratio limits, simple geometry, and mobile-friendly animation choices.

output_examples.input: Add orbit controls and bloom to an existing Three.js demo.
output: A revised interaction plan with damped camera controls, bloom settings, and a stable render loop.
Guidance for importing the required Three.js addons from npm or a pinned CDN path.

output_examples.input: Make a product viewer for a small WebGL app.
output: A viewer structure with centered model loading, realistic materials, balanced lights, and resize behavior.
A testing checklist for model scale, camera distance, shadows, and browser performance.

best_practices: Start with the scene graph, then add objects, lights, controls, and animation in separate steps.
Reuse geometries and materials, cap pixel ratio, and keep animation loops focused on transforms.
Use modern ES module imports and pin external dependency versions for repeatable builds.
anti_patterns: Do not create new geometry or materials inside every animation frame.
Do not rely on legacy global Three.js APIs when using modern module imports.
Do not ship CDN-based examples without considering availability, version pinning, and local bundling.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build browser-based Three.js scenes, demos, viewers, and interactive 3D app patterns.

faq.question: Does it create complete production apps?
faq.answer: It provides implementation patterns and guidance, but production apps still need testing, assets, and integration work.

faq.question: Can it use GLTF or GLB models?
faq.answer: Yes. The reference material includes model loading guidance with GLTFLoader and scene centering techniques.

faq.question: Does it support camera controls?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains OrbitControls setup, damping, update timing, and modern import paths.

faq.question: Can it improve performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers pixel ratio caps, geometry reuse, instancing, shadow settings, and simpler geometry choices.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Some examples use pinned CDN imports. Production projects can replace them with local npm package imports.
